proposals.before: Its soil soil; lower soil loam.
proposals.after: Its soil was soil; the lower soil was rich loam.
proposals.reason: Literal repeats “soil” unnaturally and under-translates 墳壚; clarify upland versus richer lowland soil.
Here 嗟 marks assent, not lament; “Alas” misreads Shun’s approving reply.

proposals.before: Yu said, "I marry Tushan on xinren, guijia, bore Qi I not treat as son, thereby able complete earth-water merit.
proposals.after: Yu said, "I married at Tushan on the days xin and ren; on gui and jia [Qi] was born, and I did not act as a [doting] father to my son, and thereby could complete the flood works."
proposals.reason: Literal is broken English and obscures the xin-ren/gui-jia day sequence and 予不子.

proposals.before: Kongjia granted him the surname Dragon-tamer and received the Shiwei as his fief.
proposals.after: Kongjia granted him the surname Dragon-tamer, and he received the succession of the Shiwei.
proposals.reason: 受豕韋之後 means receiving the Shiwei line’s succession, not that Kongjia received Shiwei as his own fief.

proposals.before: Fa died and his son Lügui became the tyrant Jie.
proposals.after: Fa died and his son Lügui was established; this was Jie.
proposals.reason: Chinese 是為桀 only identifies Lügui as Jie; 'tyrant' is not in the source and invents a moral label.

decisions.after: Its soil was soft loam; the lower soil was fertile clay.
decisions.reason: 其土壤，下土墳壚 is broken as “Its soil soil,” and the proposal’s “Its soil was soil” still fails to render 壤 as a soil grade. 壤 is soft/loamy earth and 墳壚 the richer lower clay, so both halves need that quality wording.
After the Four Peaks recommend Yu, 舜曰：「嗟，然！」is approving assent (matching the following charge to Yu), not lament; “Alas” misreads 嗟, and “Ah—yes!” restores the approving interjection.

decisions.after: Yu said, "I married a woman of Tushan on the days xin and ren; on gui and jia Qi was born, and I did not treat him as a son, and thereby could complete the earth-and-water works."
decisions.reason: The before text is ungrammatical and the xin-ren / gui-jia sequence plus 予不子 must be repaired, but the proposal’s “married at Tushan” turns 娶涂山 into a wedding place, and the bracketed “[doting]” / “[Qi]” glosses invent tone not in the literal. Keep the day-pair reading and render 娶涂山 as marrying a woman of Tushan, 生啟 as Qi’s birth, and 予不子 as not treating him as a son.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 予（辛壬）娶涂山，［辛壬］癸甲，生啟予不子，以故能成水土功

decisions.reason: In 孔甲賜之姓曰御龍氏，受豕韋之後 the implied subject of 受 is Liu Lei (之), who receives the Shiwei line’s succession; the before text wrongly makes Kongjia the one who “received the Shiwei as his fief.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 孔甲賜之姓曰御龍氏，受豕韋之後

decisions.reason: 帝發崩，子帝履癸立，是為桀 only records Fa’s death, Lügui’s accession, and the identification 是為桀; “tyrant” is not in the Chinese and invents a moral label the unit does not state.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 帝發崩，子帝履癸立，是為桀
